title: write-ahead buffer: stage inbound articles to local FS before IPFS write
description:
Why: The ingestion queue already decouples peer-facing acceptance from pipeline processing, but if rust-ipfs write throughput is the bottleneck, articles queue up in memory and slow peers see backpressure. A durable write-ahead buffer accepts articles to fast local storage first, returns success to the sending peer immediately, then drains to IPFS asynchronously. This also provides crash recovery: articles staged but not yet written to IPFS survive a process restart.

The window between acceptance and IPFS write must be handled: if a client requests an article that is staged but not yet in IPFS, the server must serve it from the staging area.

What:
Add a configurable on-disk write-ahead staging area for inbound articles:
- On article acceptance (IHAVE/TAKETHIS/POST): write raw article bytes to a staging file, record (staging_id, message_id, file_path, received_at) in a SQLite staging table, return success to peer.
- A drain task reads from the staging table in order and writes each article through the normal pipeline (IPFS put, msgid_map, group_log, gossip). On success, delete the staging file and remove the row.
- On process restart: re-queue any rows still in the staging table — they were accepted but not drained.
- If a protocol handler receives a request for a message_id that is in the staging table but not yet in IPFS, serve the raw bytes directly from the staging file.

Configuration (new [staging] section in config):
  [staging]
  path = "/var/spool/usenet-ipfs/staging"  # directory for staging files
  max_bytes = 5_368_709_120               # max total staging area size in bytes (default 5 GiB)
  max_entries = 500_000                   # max number of staged articles (default 500K)
  # If either limit is reached, new articles are rejected with 436 (try again later)
  # rather than silently dropped.
  # Omit [staging] section to use the in-memory ingestion queue only (current behaviour).

Implementation notes:
- Staging files named by staging_id (UUID or sequence number) not message_id, to avoid filesystem issues with message_id special characters.
- The staging SQLite table lives in the transit database (not core) alongside the existing articles table.
- Drain concurrency: configurable drain_workers (default 1) to control IPFS write parallelism.
- The staging area is not a cache — entries are deleted once successfully drained to IPFS.
